# Llama Stack GA-Readiness Assessment

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps
between current Llama Stack Tech Preview quality and the GA bar. It produces
the definitive GA scope that all stability and hardening work is sized
against, drawn from a systematic assessment of TP feedback scattered across
support tickets plus direct evaluation of the component.

## Scope

- Inventory gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar across the four
  areas named by the strategy: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
  and error handling.
- Collect and consolidate TP feedback from support tickets into a single
  gap register.
- Validate findings against the deployed Llama Stack distribution
  (LlamaStackDistribution CR, OpenAI-compatible REST APIs, provider plugins)
  as described in the platform architecture context.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: prioritized gap list with
  severity, affected surfaces, and recommended disposition (fix for GA,
  accept with known-issue, or defer), so downstream stability and
  hardening work can be planned against it.
- Explicitly identify any gaps that fall outside the four named areas but
  would block a GA support posture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA-readiness assessment document exists covering all four gap areas
  (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling) with a
  pass/fail verdict per area against the GA bar.
- The TP support-ticket feedback has been systematically reviewed and every
  relevant ticket is reflected in the gap register.
- The assessment produces a definitive GA scope: every gap is classified
  (fix for GA / known-issue / defer) with a severity rating, and the
  stability and hardening workload can be derived from it without further
  discovery.
- Findings that change the scope or approach of downstream stability,
  hardening, or support-posture work are called out explicitly as gating
  outcomes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between
  current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
  error handling), producing the definitive GA scope.

# Llama Stack API Stability Guarantee and Tested Upgrade Path

## Description

This epic delivers the API stability guarantee that GA requires for the
published Llama Stack API surface: versioned APIs, a deprecation policy, and
a tested upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases. It is the
primary code-level hardening work of the GA graduation and is scoped by the
GA-readiness assessment.

## Description of Dependence

This epic starts once the GA-readiness assessment has produced the
definitive GA scope; the assessment's API-stability and upgrade-path findings
determine the exact scope of this work. If the assessment finds the gap
smaller or larger than estimated, this epic's scope is rewritten accordingly.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published Llama Stack API surface (the
  OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the LlamaStackDistribution CRD), with the
  versioning scheme and deprecation policy documented.
- Implement deprecation handling per the policy (versioned endpoints,
  migration guidance for deprecated surface).
- Implement and test the upgrade path from the last two TP releases to the
  GA release, covering distribution CR upgrades and API-consumer migration.
- Close the API-stability gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment
  for the fix-for-GA disposition.
- Ensure the build pipeline is green for all changes (component is already
  Konflux-onboarded).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published APIs are versioned and the versioning is enforced in code, not
  convention.
- A deprecation policy document exists and deprecated surface follows it
  (announced, documented, removable per policy).
- An upgrade from each of the last two TP releases to the GA release is
  exercised by automated tests and succeeds without manual intervention
  beyond documented steps.
- Every API-stability gap marked fix-for-GA in the GA-readiness assessment
  is closed or explicitly reclassified with rationale.
- The build pipeline is green for the Llama Stack midstream repositories.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Published API surface carries a stability guarantee:
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the
  last two TP releases.

## Risks / Notes

- Scope is an estimate until the GA-readiness assessment lands; this epic
  is gated on that assessment (scope rewrite on outcome).
- The deprecation and stability commitment requires product review before
  publication.

# Llama Stack Production Support Posture

## Description

This epic puts the production support posture in place for Llama Stack GA:
documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration
matrix. The deliverables are support-policy artifacts that define what Red
Hat supports and at what service level once the component graduates from
Tech Preview.

## Description of Dependence

This epic starts once the GA-readiness assessment has produced the
definitive GA scope; the assessment's findings on scale limits,
error handling, and upgrade paths determine the content of the supported
configuration matrix and the SLO targets. If those findings change, this
epic's scope is rewritten accordingly.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the supported GA distribution
  (informed by the assessment's scale-limit and error-handling findings).
- Define and document the backport policy: which releases receive fixes,
  for how long, and how security and critical fixes are handled.
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix: supported
  provider combinations, deployment sizes, scale limits, and platform
  versions for GA.
- Include the TrustyAI guardrails integration in the supported
  configuration matrix as a supported configuration for Llama Stack GA
  distributions, coordinated with the guardrails promotion stream so the
  promoted integration is inside the supported envelope at GA.
- Align the support posture with the platform's existing GA support
  conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented and reviewed, covering availability and
  operational service levels for the supported configuration.
- The backport policy is documented and covers the GA release and the
  supported TP-to-GA upgrade window.
- The supported configuration matrix enumerates supported provider plugins,
  deployment/scale limits, and platform versions, and includes the TrustyAI
  guardrails integration as a supported configuration; configurations
  outside the matrix are explicitly marked unsupported.
- Every scale-limit and error-handling gap marked fix-for-GA or
  known-issue in the GA-readiness assessment is reflected in the matrix or
  SLO targets.
- Support-organization stakeholders have reviewed and accepted the
  posture documents.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: Production support posture is in place: documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

## Risks / Notes

- SLO targets and backport policy are organizational commitments requiring
  product/support sign-off — budget review time.
- Content depends on the GA-readiness assessment outcome; this epic is
  gated on that assessment (scope rewrite on outcome).

# TrustyAI Guardrails as Supported Llama Stack Integration

## Description

This epic promotes safety guardrails via TrustyAI from an experimental flag
to a supported, documented integration for Llama Stack GA distributions.
After this epic, a user configuring a Llama Stack distribution with TrustyAI
guardrails is on a supported path with documentation, rather than behind a
TP opt-in.

## Scope

- Promote the TrustyAI guardrails integration in the Llama Stack
  distribution from experimental/opt-in status to supported: the
  integration is part of the supported configuration, not gated behind an
  experimental flag.
- Wire and validate the guardrails path end to end: Llama Stack safety
  surface consuming TrustyAI services (TrustyAIService CR) in a supported
  configuration.
- Coordinate with the TrustyAI team's validation work: the TrustyAI-side
  validation of the guardrails integration is owned and tracked by the
  TrustyAI team as their own work item (TrustyAI is passive here — no
  TrustyAI code changes — but the validating team differs, so the validation
  is not an acceptance criterion on this epic). This epic supplies the
  supported configuration surface and the integrated path that the
  validation exercises, and receives its findings.
- Provide engineering input for the customer-facing guardrails documentation:
  the supported configuration surface, setup steps, and usage behavior,
  verified accurate against the implementation and handed to the Llama Stack
  GA documentation uplift stream as technical reference material. The
  customer-facing content itself is authored in the documentation stream,
  not in this epic.
- Ensure the build pipeline is green for all changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Llama Stack GA distribution can be configured with TrustyAI guardrails
  without any experimental flag, and that configuration is within the
  supported configuration matrix.
- The end-to-end guardrails path (Llama Stack safety API surface backed by
  a TrustyAI service) is validated and covered by automated tests.
- Engineering input for the customer-facing guardrails documentation
  (supported configuration, setup, usage) is delivered to the documentation
  stream and is accurate against the implementation.
- The change is reversible: the guardrails integration remains an opt-in
  configuration — a Llama Stack GA distribution can be configured without
  TrustyAI guardrails and remains inside the supported configuration
  envelope (the promotion adds a supported path; it does not enable
  guardrails by default).
- No experimental/TP opt-in gate remains for the guardrails integration in
  GA distributions.
- The build pipeline is green for the changed repositories.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported,
  documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

## Risks / Notes

- The strategy does not state what changes on the TrustyAI side; this epic
  treats TrustyAI as a passive component (existing service, keeps working).
  The TrustyAI-team-owned validation of the guardrails integration is
  tracked as a separate TrustyAI-owned validation work item, since the
  validating team differs from this epic's owning team — work controlled by
  another team is not closed as an acceptance criterion here. If
  TrustyAI-side code changes are needed, that work is likewise TrustyAI
  owned.
- The promotion touches safety-relevant behavior, but the integration
  remains user-configured: users opt in by configuring TrustyAI guardrails
  in their distribution, so this epic adds a supported path rather than
  flipping a default. The TrustyAI-side validation verdict is delivered by
  the TrustyAI team's validation work item, which depends on this epic.
- Cross-stream coordination: the first acceptance criterion requires the
  guardrails configuration to be within the supported configuration matrix,
  which is authored by the production support posture stream. That stream
  owns adding the TrustyAI guardrails integration to the matrix; this epic
  provides the supported configuration surface as input.

# Dashboard Llama Stack Management On by Default

## Description

This epic makes the Dashboard enable Llama Stack management by default for
entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. Llama Stack
management surfaces (navigation, resource views, and management actions for
LlamaStackDistribution resources) become available out of the box for
clusters with the appropriate entitlement.

## Scope

- Remove the TP opt-in gate for Llama Stack management in the Dashboard:
  the feature is enabled by default for entitled clusters.
- Implement entitlement-based gating so the default enablement applies
  only to clusters with the appropriate entitlement.
- Follow the existing Dashboard pattern for per-component feature flags
  and defaults (OdhDashboardConfig CR), per the platform architecture
  context.
- Update affected captions, labels, and status text that currently
  advertise Tech Preview status for Llama Stack management (incidental to
  this change, no new content authored).

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster, Llama Stack management is available in the
  Dashboard with no opt-in configuration required.
- On a cluster without the entitlement, Llama Stack management remains
  hidden/disabled.
- The opt-in flag no longer gates the feature; existing opt-in
  configurations continue to work without regression.
- The change is reversible: a configuration path exists to disable Llama
  Stack management in the Dashboard (rollback safety for a
  default-behavior change).
- No TP-preview labeling remains on the default-enabled Llama Stack
  management surfaces.
- The build pipeline is green for the Dashboard repositories.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default
  for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

## Risks / Notes

- This epic runs in parallel with the Llama Stack GA hardening work
  (different repositories; the Dashboard integrates via Kubernetes CRs,
  not shared build artifacts). Coordinate the default flip to land with
  the GA announcement so TP-quality Llama Stack is not exposed by default
  before GA — a release-coordination note, not a dependency.

# Llama Stack GA Documentation Uplift

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards, including
migration notes from Tech Preview. It produces the customer-facing
documentation that describes the GA-supported API surface, support
posture, guardrails integration, and Dashboard experience, and tells
existing TP users how to migrate.

## Scope
